fixture_name: Four-lane arterial improvement — US preliminary design (FHWA case study, PD)
subject: judge-baseline

justifications.substance: Closely-spaced intersection queuing, turning, and parking interference is a genuine preliminary-design safety issue with concrete design levers (movement restrictions, stall placement) on a corridor flagged for accident history.
justifications.evidence_grounding: Pivotal claim is anchored by the verbatim EV-US-016 quote matching the scenario nearly word-for-word; peripheral additions ('recorded high-accident designations', 'specified' stalls) go beyond the quote but do not displace the grounded core.
justifications.jurisdiction_correctness: Properly typed as safety_concern with null normative basis and no compliance mandate conflated into it, keeping FHWA RSA safety semantics clean.
justifications.recommendation_quality: Offers two actionable, viable design-stage measures—turning-movement restrictions and relocating stalls outside the intersection functional area—though it stops short of naming specific approaches or movements.
justifications.vru_coverage: Pedestrians and cyclists are explicitly acknowledged as potentially present on the commercial corridor, then scoped out on the stated rationale that the conflict mechanism is vehicle-to-vehicle; acknowledged-but-not-central treatment merits 1 per rubric.

justifications.substance: Queue storage and coordination between signals 650 ft apart on a corridor with recorded high-accident status is a classic, substantive preliminary-design-stage RSA concern with real collision mechanisms (spillback blockage, unexpected queue discharge).
justifications.evidence_grounding: The pivotal claim (signal separation distance) is supported by a verbatim quote from EV-US-001; the derived spillback inference is labelled as such and the corridor crash history traces to the recorded case-study input cited in the confidence basis.
justifications.jurisdiction_correctness: Correctly filed as a safety_concern distinct from any compliance question, appropriate to the preliminary-design stage under FHWA RSA practice, with framework semantics respected throughout.
justifications.recommendation_quality: Recommendation names concrete, viable measures (signal coordination/interconnection, Do Not Block Intersection signing, conspicuity upgrades for signal displays), complementing the statement's check-queue-storage action.
justifications.vru_coverage: Pedestrians and cyclists are explicitly acknowledged with a stated rationale for scoping road users to vehicle occupants, whose exposure the spillback mechanism genuinely centres on; a fuller treatment of VRU effects (e.g., spillback encroaching on crosswalks) would strengthen it further.
